title: Social Searcher Alternatives: Free & Budget Listening in 2026
summary: Social Searcher is the default answer to "free social listening," but its real monitoring tier caps at 100 searches a day and a single alert, and most of the free tools people once paired with it have gone paid-only. This guide sorts what's a trial in disguise, covers what happened to Mention, BuzzSumo, Hootsuite, and TweetDeck/X Pro, and explains when it's time to move past text-based tools altogether.
body_markdown:
As of September 2026, only two social listening tools remain both fully free and unrestricted for ongoing use — Google Alerts and Talkwalker Alerts — and both are email-alert tools with no dashboard, sentiment analysis, or video coverage. If you're searching for social searcher alternatives because its "completely free" branding only covers ad-hoc lookups (the real monitoring product caps at 100 searches a day and 1 alert), know this: every other tool once known for a free tier — Mention, BuzzSumo, Hootsuite, TweetDeck/X Pro — has discontinued or paywalled it since 2023.


Social Searcher is the name everyone reaches for when they want "free social listening." Its own free tier is thinner than most people assume.


The homepage still says "completely free... unlimited searches... no caps." That phrase only covers one-off keyword lookups — not the monitoring and alerts product most teams actually need. The real free tier caps at 100 searches a day and a single email alert.


Meanwhile, half the budget tools people used to pair with Social Searcher have quietly disappeared. Mention killed its self-serve plans in July 2025. BuzzSumo dropped its free tier entirely, and Hootsuite's has been gone since 2023.


This piece breaks down what Social Searcher's free tier really gives you, which social searcher alternatives are still genuinely free in 2026, which ones quietly went paid-only, and when it's time to stop patching together free tools and move to a real platform.\\


## Before You Look for Social Searcher Alternatives: What Does the Free Tier Actually Give You?


**Genuinely free** : no credit card required, no time limit, and core search or alert functionality usable indefinitely at zero cost. That's different from a **free trial** (time-boxed — you upgrade or lose access) and a **freemium teaser** (technically free forever, but capped so low it can't support real ongoing monitoring). Social Searcher's free tier lands in the third category. It's real, but thin.


Here's the actual tier breakdown, confirmed via a direct fetch of a third-party pricing listing that reproduces the vendor's own table (Source:[Techjockey, 2026](https://www.techjockey.com/detail/social-searcher) ):

Platform coverage spans Facebook, X/Twitter, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Telegram, plus web, forum, and blog mentions. There's no dedicated Reddit monitoring tier, and TikTok/Instagram coverage is search-based rather than deep video analysis. You won't get transcription, view-based ranking, or Reels/Shorts-specific metrics on any tier.


Three things break once a team tries to actually run on this:


-


The genuinely-free tier caps at **100 searches a day and 1 email alert** — unusable for tracking more than one keyword set.


-


"Unlimited free search" only applies to live, uncached lookups. Saved history and export require Standard or Professional.


-


API access reportedly starts around $49/mo, per third-party pricing trackers — Social Searcher doesn't appear to publish a standalone pricing page, so treat that figure as an estimate rather than a confirmed rate.


## Which Social Listening Tools Are Still Genuinely Free in 2026?


Two tools pass the genuinely-free test with no asterisks: Google Alerts and Talkwalker Alerts. Both have stayed stable for years, and both come with a hard ceiling.


**Google Alerts** is fully free, with no caps and no credit card, ever. The catch: a 24–72 hour indexing delay before results show up, no dashboard, no export, and — the big one — **zero social media coverage** . It watches news and the open web only, not a single social platform (Source:[Google Alerts, 2026](https://alerts.google.com/) ).


**Talkwalker Alerts** covers more ground but still isn't a social listening dashboard. It offers unlimited alerts by email or RSS, with only digest frequency limited. Coverage spans news, blogs, forums, and websites, plus X/Twitter mentions — but not Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube (Source:[Talkwalker Alerts, 2026](https://www.talkwalker.com/alerts-social-search) ). Talkwalker's full paid Social Listening product exists behind a demo-only, quote-based sales process.


Both tools do one job well: catching a mention before it snowballs, not analyzing it. That makes them genuinely useful for light PR monitoring — did a journalist mention your brand, did a competitor get written up somewhere new. Neither gives you sentiment scoring, a dashboard to browse history in, or any video coverage at all. If your brand's conversation lives on TikTok or in Reels, these two tools are functionally blind to it.


## Which "Free" Social Listening Tools Have Quietly Gone Paid-Only?


This is the part most "free tools" roundups miss. Nearly every other tool that built its reputation on a free or budget tier has killed it, capped it, or repriced it since 2023.


**Mention** discontinued its self-serve Solo, Pro, and Pro Plus plans in **July 2025** . As of September 2026, its pricing page shows a single enterprise "Company Plan" and nothing else (Source:[Mention, 2026](https://mention.com/en/pricing/) ). Older claims that "Mention has a free plan with 1,000 mentions" are stale — don't repeat them. It's also reportedly priced around $599/mo annually, per third-party aggregator figures not shown on the live pricing page itself.


**BuzzSumo's** free plan is gone entirely. It now offers a 7-day trial with no credit card, and its cheapest paid tier starts at **$199/mo for a single user** , climbing to $999/mo (Source: BuzzSumo pricing trackers, 2026).


**Hootsuite** killed its free plan in **2023** . Today it's a 14-day trial only, and the cheapest paid plan runs **$99 per user, per month** , billed annually (Source:[Hootsuite, 2026](https://www.hootsuite.com/plans/) ).


**TweetDeck/X Pro** is the real scoop here. It was free until 2023, then moved behind X Premium ($8/mo) in August 2023. On **March 26, 2026** , it moved again — this time behind **X Premium+ at roughly $40/mo** — with no advance warning (Source: aggregator pricing trackers, 2026). Monitoring X/Twitter through the official interface now costs five times what it did three years ago, yet plenty of roundups still list it as free.


**Social Mention** (socialmention.com) is widely reported as abandoned — repeated direct attempts to load the site failed to connect, though that's not the same as a confirmed shutdown notice. Here's the twist: BrandMentions now runs its own free-but-limited search page under the "Social Mention" name as a lead-gen tool for its paid subscription. That page is not the original tool, and it shouldn't be recommended as if it were.

## When Do Social Searcher Alternatives Stop Being Enough?


Once you've outgrown Google Alerts and Talkwalker Alerts, and Social Searcher's 100 searches a day feel too thin, the next step is usually a budget paid platform. **Awario** (from about $29/mo), **Mentionlytics** , **BrandMentions** , and **Brand24** (up to about $199/mo) cover far more ground than any free tool — see[the full pricing breakdown](https://syncly.app/blog/mentionlytics-vs-brand24-vs-awario-budget-social-listening) for the exact tiers. For a broader survey of budget-friendly options,[our startup tool roundup](https://syncly.app/blog/best-social-listening-tools-for-startups-and-small-teams-2026) covers the category in more depth.


All of these tools — free, budget, and Social Searcher's own paid tiers included — share one gap. They're built for text-based mention tracking, not video content. None of them transcribe a TikTok, rank content by view performance, or analyze what's actually happening inside a Reel or a Short.

Once monitoring volume goes beyond a few hundred mentions or a handful of keyword alerts, or once a team needs real video-content performance data instead of an inbox full of email digests, free and budget text tools stop being the right tool for the job.

## Key Takeaways


-


Social Searcher's real free tier caps at 100 searches a day and 1 email alert — its "unlimited free" claim only covers ad-hoc lookups, not ongoing monitoring.


-


Google Alerts and Talkwalker Alerts are the only tools left that are genuinely free with no restrictions, and both lack a dashboard, sentiment scoring, or video coverage.


-


Mention, BuzzSumo, Hootsuite, and TweetDeck/X Pro have all discontinued or repriced their free tiers since 2023.


-


The "Social Mention" name is now used by BrandMentions as a lead-gen page — the original tool is widely reported as defunct.


-


Once a brand needs video-native coverage or monitoring beyond a handful of keywords, it's time to move past free tools entirely.


Verdict: if you want something that's actually free forever, your 2026 options are Google Alerts and Talkwalker Alerts, full stop. Everything else — including Social Searcher's own real product — charges for meaningful monitoring, and half the field has quietly repriced or shut down since 2023.


That's not necessarily bad news. Free tools were never built to carry a brand's entire monitoring workload.


They were built to catch the occasional mention, not to analyze a conversation. The real question isn't which free tool survives longest. It's whether your brand has outgrown text-only mention tracking altogether, especially if your audience lives on TikTok and Reels.
